title: A timestamp a client sends carries its UTC offset
intent: A date and time without a UTC offset names no instant: ten in the morning is a different moment in every zone. Stored as if it were UTC, it puts a writer in any other zone off by that zone's offset, and nothing reports it. The published API contract already asks for the offset, since a date-time there is the RFC 3339 form, whose offset is required. So timestamp text without one is refused wherever a request schema reads it, a route parameter takes a type that refuses it too, and a declared filter refuses a bound without one; the refusal names the fix. An app whose route reads a timestamp nothing refuses that way does not start. Reading a value without an offset as UTC, for a sender known to send UTC without saying so, is the framework's one way around it, and it is an escape a person decides and a reviewer sees. So is an app's own validator that reads the text before the timestamp's type does, since it can read the time in a zone of its own choosing. The wall time of a named zone needs neither: the zone names the instant, and the framework's type for it refuses a time the clocks skip or repeat.
reference: The rule fails closed by name. Every reference to NaiveMeansUtc is refused: as a name, as an attribute (core.NaiveMeansUtc, terp.core.NaiveMeansUtc), through getattr with that literal name, and in a string Pydantic evaluates as a type, such as a quoted annotation, a forward reference in Optional["NaiveMeansUtc"] or a field handed to create_model. So is every name the file binds to it by an import alias, an assignment or a type alias, at each use where that binding is the one in scope, and a class attribute bound to it at each use of that attribute's name, through the class, a subclass or an instance. A class or a re-export of that name from anywhere counts too, and so does reaching terp.core.timestamps, the boundary's own module, however it is spelled (an import of it, from terp.core import timestamps, an attribute of the terp.core package or a getattr of it by that literal name, and its dotted name written as a literal, as importlib and sys.modules are handed it); an attribute called timestamps on anything else, or on a local that shadows the package's name, is the app's own. A Literal value is text, not the escape. A plain datetime field of a BaseSchema needs nothing: at run time BaseSchema refuses timestamp text without an offset wherever it reads a datetime itself, as a 422 at its place. A route parameter, and a field of a class that reads its own fields (a plain model, a Pydantic dataclass, a table), is typed Instant, which puts the same refusal in front of it, and create_app refuses to start while a route reads a timestamp with none (ADR 0208). A declared filter refuses a bound without one as a 400 that names it, reading a bound given as text first (ADR 0206). The rule holds every root that ships Python, a worker as much as the app; terp.core, which defines the boundary and its escape, and terp.arch, which defines this rule and names both as the data it matches, are neither's user. An app's own validator that runs before a timestamp's type is the escape too (ADR 0207). That is a BeforeValidator, WrapValidator or PlainValidator, or a name bound to one, in an Annotated type that reads a timestamp (datetime, AwareDatetime and the other datetime types, and Instant, in a union, a list or a quoted annotation), counted where that type is spelled and at each use of a name bound to it, as each use of NaiveMeansUtc counts; and a field_validator in before, wrap or plain mode, or Pydantic 1's validator with pre=True, written as a decorator or a call in the body of a class or of a base the same file defines, on a field that class or one of those bases declares as a timestamp, named, as "*", or by a field name or a mode the file computes. Each of those names is followed through the file's imports and assignments: an alias of Annotated, of a validator or of field_validator, and a type alias over a timestamp, NewType and TypeAliasType included. An after validator, a validator on a field that is no timestamp (a date is a day), and a model validator, which sees the body rather than a field, are not. The wall time of a place is LocalTimeIn's (Annotated[datetime, LocalTimeIn("Europe/Amsterdam")]), which names the instant and refuses a time the clocks skip or repeat, so it is no escape; it refuses a zone that names no place, so UTC under any name stays NaiveMeansUtc's.

runtime.rationale: The schema holds the invariant itself. BaseSchema puts the refusal in front of every datetime it validates itself, following every definition the schema refers to: in a field, a list, a mapping, a union, a type alias, a stdlib dataclass or a TypedDict, under the name Pydantic reads it by, and a nested BaseSchema holds its own; so timestamp text without a UTC offset is a 422 at its place. A declared filter refuses a bound without one as a 400 that names the filter. A class that brings its own Pydantic validator, a plain model, a Pydantic dataclass or a table, reads its own fields, as a request model that is not a BaseSchema does. A class that takes either hook the base relies on from anywhere but BaseSchema is refused when it is defined. The worker's trust in the text it wrote is a context variable, and the refusal's and the escape's nodes are known by their own functions, all in a module the build-time half refuses to an app. The build-time half governs the framework's one way around the refusal, so taking it is never quiet. The early-validator half is build-time by decision (ADR 0207): an app's own validator runs in front of the refusal, so its reading of a time without an offset reaches the refusal as an instant, and although the schema walk could see a before or wrap validator around a timestamp, it cannot tell one a person marked from one they did not, since the marker is a comment in the source. LocalTimeIn, which reads the wall time of the place a field declares, is the framework's way to take such a time, and its own node is known to the walk by its reader's function, as the escape's is. What a BaseSchema does not read itself, a route parameter and a class that reads its own fields as a request body or nested in one, create_app checks once every router is mounted (ADR 0208): it walks the schema each route reads each parameter with and refuses to start while a timestamp stands behind none of the refusal, Instant, LocalTimeIn, the escape or an aware-only datetime, naming each one and the fix.
